primary_source_statements.paraphrase: Five lit-unlit replicate pairs established June 2024; mean illuminance 4.52 +/- 0.23 SEM lux.
Factorial light x open, bagged, day-only, night-only access; 20 plants reported per combination; exact distribution among plot pairs not clarified.
Three to five mature fruits per sampled plant; seed set is developed seeds divided by total ovules per fruit.

P. kansuensis pollen drops 23.09% under open access and 53.80% under night-only access. Seed decline is reported for night-only rather than other two treatments. No significant pollen or seed effects reported for E. regelii.
Total visits similar but guild composition changes; 56.0% seed reduction discussed with the nocturnal pathway; per-visit pollination efficiency not measured.
Captions distinguish significant solid versus nonsignificant dashed lines in Figures 4-5 and label error bars SEM. Images not visually verified in this retrieval.

interpretation_limits: No raw plant-level data or fitted coefficients recovered
No direct comparative species-by-light effect reestimated
Non-significance is not equivalence or zero effect
Selfing capacity and night-visitor reliance are confounded with species identity
Night-only seed penalty must not become an open-access whole-plant seed penalty
